old_title: Cheaper AutoCAD Alternatives to Try in 2026
old_content:
Quick answer: This guide compares six alternatives to AutoCAD, with prices copied from each official website. Free options: BricsCAD, DraftSight, LibreCAD and SolidWorks. Paid plans start at €5 one-time (FreeCAD). For comparison, AutoCAD itself costs $175/month. Use the table below to match price and free plan to your budget.

Last checked: November 7, 2026. Based on each tool's official website and pricing pages. Prices and features change, so confirm details on the official site before you buy.

Exploring AutoCAD Alternatives for Freelancers and Small Teams

For many freelancers and small design teams, the investment in professional CAD software is a critical decision. Autodesk AutoCAD, known for its "faster, smarter 2D and 3D drafting Powered by Autodesk AI," comes with a starting price of $175/month. This cost, alongside specific workflow needs, often prompts a search for "AutoCAD alternatives." My goal here is to help you weigh your options accurately before making a purchase.

AutoCAD at a Glance

  • Price Model: Freemium
  • Best For: 2D and 3D drafting with AI assistance.

Alternative CAD Software Options

BricsCAD

Octave BricsCAD is professional CAD software for designers, innovators, and engineers. It offers a unique DWG-based approach to enhance productivity in design processes. BricsCAD has a free plan and paid options from €330 one-time.

It fits users seeking flexible 2D and 3D CAD. Before buying, verify which platforms it supports, as I could not find this information on the pages I checked.

DraftSight

DraftSight is 2D CAD design and drafting software, backed by SOLIDWORKS. It aims for precision and offers realistic pricing. DraftSight provides a free plan and paid versions from $299/year.

This tool suits those needing reliable 2D CAD. I could not find which platforms DraftSight supports on the pages I checked.

FreeCAD

FreeCAD is an open-source 3D parametric modeler. It is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux. FreeCAD costs €5 one-time for its open-source edition.

This is ideal for users seeking a community-supported, cross-platform 3D modeling solution. Its strength is being an open-source option for parametric design.

LibreCAD

LibreCAD is a free open-source 2D CAD application. It supports Windows, Apple (macOS), Linux, and Web platforms. LibreCAD is Free (open-source) and offers support through its large, dedicated community.

It's a strong choice for users needing basic 2D CAD without cost. Its broad platform support makes it accessible.

SolidWorks

SOLIDWORKS provides software solutions for 3D CAD, design, and product development. It helps innovators create and collaborate on product experiences. SOLIDWORKS has a free plan for students.

It suits teams focused on comprehensive 3D design and AI capabilities. I could not find which platforms it supports on the pages I checked.

Fusion 360

Autodesk Fusion is cloud-based 3D CAD, CAM, CAE, and PCB software. It is listed as "Free software" with paid plans from $57/month. Fusion 360 is suitable for users needing an integrated, cloud-powered design solution. Its strength is combining multiple design functionalities in one platform.

Pros and Cons of Considering Alternatives

For AutoCAD

  • ✅ Offers 2D and 3D drafting, powered by Autodesk AI.
  • ✅ Provides a free plan.
  • ✅ A free trial is available.
  • ❌ Starting price of $175/month (or $260/month for a monthly subscription, $2,095/year for an annual subscription) might be a significant investment.

For Alternatives

  • ✅ Many alternatives offer free plans or are entirely free and open-source.
  • ✅ Options like LibreCAD and FreeCAD explicitly mention supporting multiple operating systems.
  • ✅ Some alternatives offer one-time purchase options, potentially saving money long-term.
  • ❌ Feature sets may vary significantly compared to AutoCAD's comprehensive offering.
  • ❌ Support for certain platforms is not always explicitly stated on alternative product pages.

When considering CAD software, prioritize tools that align with your primary drafting needs and budget. Free plans or open-source options can be excellent starting points.

Who Should Stay with AutoCAD

You should consider staying with AutoCAD if your workflow specifically benefits from "faster, smarter 2D and 3D drafting Powered by Autodesk AI." If your projects demand the specific features and integrations offered by Autodesk's ecosystem, the investment might be justified. Teams already familiar with AutoCAD's interface may also benefit from avoiding a learning curve with new software.

Recommendations for Different Needs

  • Cheapest Option: For users prioritizing cost, LibreCAD is Free (open-source) and offers 2D CAD for Windows, Apple, Linux, and Web. FreeCAD is also highly affordable at €5 one-time for its open-source 3D parametric modeler.
  • Easiest to Start With: Both LibreCAD and DraftSight offer free plans, making them accessible to try. LibreCAD's community support can also aid new users. DraftSight mentions being "familiar" for 2D CAD.
  • Most Powerful Alternative: For comprehensive 3D design and development, SOLIDWORKS offers solutions trusted by innovators and includes AI capabilities in its 2027 version. Autodesk Fusion 360, with its cloud-based 3D CAD, CAM, CAE, and PCB capabilities, is also a powerful option, starting from $57/month.

Common Questions About CAD Software

Does AutoCAD offer a free version for freelancers?

Yes, AutoCAD does offer a free plan. Additionally, a free trial is available for users to explore its capabilities before committing to a paid subscription.

What are the typical costs for AutoCAD?

AutoCAD has a starting monthly price of $175. For more specific plans, an annual subscription costs $2,095, while a monthly subscription is $260.

Can AutoCAD be used for both 2D and 3D design?

Yes, AutoCAD is described as offering "faster, smarter 2D and 3D drafting." It is powered by Autodesk AI to assist with routine tasks in both dimensions.

What specific features or integrations are crucial for your daily CAD workflow? Consider these as you evaluate the options.
